newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia appoints new finance minister - agency.
newsitem.headline: Serbia appoints new finance minister - agency.

text.p: The Serbian parliament on Thursday elected Borislav Milacic as the new republican finance minister, state news agency Tanjug reported.
Milacic, 44, replaces Dusan Vlatkovic who has been elected governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

Proposing Milacic for the post, Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic described him as an economist with vast experience and an expert in finance and banking who held responsible jobs in Beobanka AD of Belgrade, the trade ministry, the republican institute for prices and the Belgrade City Council.
Milacic is a member of the Yugoslav Left (JUL) which forms the ruling coalition together with the Socialist Party of Serbia and New Democracy.
He is general manager of the private architectural design and construction firm Koling.
Opposition Democratic Party MPs opposed Milacic's election arguing his nomination had arrived late in parliament.
Milacic was elected by 129 votes in favour, 13 against, one abstained while four did not cast their ballot.
Of the 250 seats in Serbia's parliament, the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia has 123. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
